rules.rationale: score_setup() awards one point each for a price band, a 10 percent change threshold, a relative-volume threshold, and a 5 percent short-float floor. None of the four is a squeeze mechanic: borrow fee, days to cover, and TTM Squeeze are computed and displayed but never scored. The rubric is a usable low-float-mover discovery filter; the Prime/Subprime vocabulary asserts a conclusion its inputs cannot support.

The arithmetic is the textbook short-interest-as-percent-of-float formula and is correct. The column was renamed from 'Short Float %' to 'Short Interest %' 2h04m before the meeting; unqualified 'Short Interest' denotes an absolute share count, so the header misdescribes a ratio. The advisor's live remark that BIYA's short interest 'appears to be low, and I am not sure why' is consistent with reading a percent-of-float under that heading.

The denominator is a trailing mean of completed daily bars that correctly excludes the incomplete current bar, matching the rebuilt Phase 2C contract, and missing inputs return None with a reason rather than zero. The defect is presentation: the numerator derives from a twice-monthly FINRA filing yet is shown beside live price and volume with no reporting-period age, and the denominator came from a cache with a one-hour TTL at detection.

A missing publication time becomes the literal string 'Unknown time' and a missing title becomes 'No title', so absence is type-indistinguishable from a real value and no downstream code can filter on recency or establish whether an item existed at detection.

The application log records IB error 10089 for every symbol including BIYA: the account lacked the required market-data subscription, so the screener fell back to delayed data. Every price, change percent, and relative volume observed during the session was delayed, and the interface carried no delayed-data indicator.

Corroboration reapplies the same four-point rubric to a second provider's numbers, so agreement tests data agreement rather than rule validity. During the observed run it was moot: every corroboration call failed with DNS resolution errors, and the absence was not surfaced in the interface.

Its missing-input handling is genuinely sound: None in, None out, excluded from the composite and never treated as zero. At detection it was displayed as an independent column and did not gate Prime/Subprime, so a ticker could show a low composite score and still be labelled Prime.
